{{Short description|American academic (1935–2024)}}
[[File:A. R. Frank Wazzan, Ph.D..jpg|thumb|A. R. Frank Wazzan, Ph.D.]]
'''A. R. "Frank" Wazzan, Ph.D.''' (October 17, 1935 – October 1, 2024) was an American-Syrian academic who was Distinguished Professor, and Dean Emeritus, of the [[UCLA Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Science|Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Science]], [[University of California, Los Angeles]] ("UCLA").<ref>{{Cite web |title=A. R. Frank Wazzan |url=https://samueli.ucla.edu/people/a-r-frank-wazzan/ |access-date=2023-12-01 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=In memoriam: A.R. Frank Wazzan, 88, renowned nuclear thermal-hydraulics engineer and former dean of UCLA Samueli |url=https://newsroom.ucla.edu/stories/a-r-frank-wazzan-88-renowned-nuclear-thermal-hydraulics-engineer-former-dean-ucla-samueli |access-date=2024-12-09 |website=UCLA |language=en-us}}</ref> Wazzan was internationally recognized for his research in the areas of [[nuclear material]], [[thermal hydraulics]], and stability of [[laminar flow]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A. R. Frank Wazzan |url=https://samueli.ucla.edu/people/a-r-frank-wazzan/ |access-date=2023-12-04 |language=en-US}}</ref> He was also known for his work on the design of underwater weapons systems for the [[U.S. Navy]], and on the operation of pressurized water [[nuclear reactor]]s for commercial applications.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=DEF 14A |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/743316/000119312513385849/d568364ddef14a.htm |access-date=2023-12-04 |website=www.sec.gov}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Wazzan attended the Presbyterian American Mission School in Latakia, Syria from 1942 to 1952. From October 1953 to March 1954 he attended [[Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences|Frankfurt University]], [[Frankfurt]], [[Germany]]. In 1955, Wazzan emigrated to the United States (port of entry New York, January 26, 1955). From January 1955 to August 1955 he attended [[Geneva College]], [[Beaver Falls, Pennsylvania|Beaver Falls]], [[Pennsylvania]]. Wazzan then enrolled at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], which awarded him a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering (1959), a master's in mechanical engineering and aeronautic sciences (1961), and a doctorate in engineering science (1963).<ref>{{Cite book |last=Berkeley |first=University of California |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-QouAQAAIAAJ&q=wazzan&pg=RA1-PA68 |title=Commencement Programs |date=1962 |pages=68 |language=en}}</ref>  Note: Wazzan spent part of '57-58' at UCLA. UC Berkeley Dissertation: The Effect of Dislocation Density and Dislocation Climb on Self Diffusion in Nickel.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wazzan |first=A. R. |date=1962-08-01 |title=Analysis of Enhanced Diffusivity in Nickel |url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/3pq7f0w5 |journal=University of California, Lawrence Radiation Laboratory, Ph.D. Thesis, UCRL 10457 |language=en}}</ref>  Dissertation Committee: John E. Dorn<ref>{{Cite web |title=Management Information Systems Tree - John Emil Dorn |url=https://academictree.org/mis/peopleinfo.php?pid=835478 |access-date=2023-12-06 |website=academictree.org}}</ref> (Chairman), Frank Hauser,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Frank Hauser |url=https://senate.universityofcalifornia.edu/_files/inmemoriam/html/FrankHauser.html |access-date=2024-12-09 |website=senate.universityofcalifornia.edu}}</ref> David Judd,<ref>{{Cite web |title=11.30.98 - UC Berkeley physicist David L. Judd, an expert in fusion reactor theory, has died at the age of 75 |url=https://newsarchive.berkeley.edu/news/media/releases/98legacy/11-30-1998.html |access-date=2024-12-09 |website=newsarchive.berkeley.edu}}</ref> [[Earl R. Parker|Earl Parker]], Maurice Holt.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Maurice Holt |url=https://senate.universityofcalifornia.edu/_files/inmemoriam/html/mauriceholt.html |access-date=2024-12-09 |website=senate.universityofcalifornia.edu}}</ref>
[[File:ARFW Security Clearance - Redact.pdf|thumb|US Dept. of Defense Security Clearance]]

== Career==
Upon completing his doctorate, Wazzan accepted a position as assistant professor at UCLA where he served on the faculty for more than 40 years. He was named Associate Dean in 1981 and Dean of the School of Engineering and Applied Science in 1986, serving in that capacity until 2001.<ref>{{Cite web |title=History {{!}} UCLA Samueli School Of Engineering |url=https://samueli.ucla.edu/history/ |access-date=2023-12-01 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Vijay Dhir appointed new interim dean of engineering school |url=https://dailybruin.com/2002/02/27/vijay-dhir-appointed-new-inter/ |access-date=2023-12-04 |website=Daily Bruin}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Chang |first=Kenneth |date=1996-02-20 |title=NEXT L.A.: A look at issues, people and ideas helping to shape the emerging metropolis. : A Small World After All : UCLA engineers are creating a world of micromachines: bug-like robots, Dick Tracy watches, sensors for pilot helmets, surgical tools and more. |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1996-02-20-me-37961-story.html |access-date=2023-12-06 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In 1996, Wazzan was instrumental in establishing the graduate degree program in biomedical engineering.<ref>{{Cite web |title=History {{!}} BE |url=https://www.bioeng.ucla.edu/history/ |access-date=2023-12-01 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In addition to his academic career, Wazzan served as consultant to [[Douglas Aircraft Company|Douglas Aircraft]], [[Hughes Electron Dynamics Division (EDD)|Hughes Electrodynamics]], [[North American Rockwell]], the [[United States Atomic Energy Commission|U.S. Atomic Energy Commission]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, Emergency Preparedness Insp Rept 50-219/86-07 on 860409-10. |url=https://www.nrc.gov/docs/ML2019/ML20198D402.pdf}}</ref> [[Westinghouse Electric Corporation|Westinghouse]] Oceanics Division, the [[French Atomic Energy Commission]], [[Électricité de France]] ([[Visiting scholar|Visiting Scholar]], Office of Commissioner Atomic Energy), [[Honeywell]], and the [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] through the [[RAND Corporation]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=RAND Corp. A.R. Wazzan |url=https://www.rand.org/pubs/authors/w/wazzan_a_r.html}}</ref><ref name="auto"/> In the latter role he was granted [[Classified information|secret]], [[Classified information|top secret]], and [[Critical Nuclear Weapon Design Information|critical nuclear weapon design information]] clearances to work on the design of underwater weapon systems, study the effect of nuclear radiation on the performance of electronic materials and communication satellites, and conduct theoretical studies in methods of hardening boosters and satellites to [[laser]] and [[Directed-energy weapon|microwave weapons]].<ref name="auto"/>

== Death ==
Wazzan died on October 1, 2024, at the age of 88.<ref>[https://newsroom.ucla.edu/stories/a-r-frank-wazzan-88-renowned-nuclear-thermal-hydraulics-engineer-former-dean-ucla-samueli In memoriam: A.R. Frank Wazzan, 88, renowned nuclear thermal-hydraulics engineer and former dean of UCLA Samueli] UCLA</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
[[File:Wazzan Tree Dedication and Plaque.jpg|thumb|Wazzan Plaque Outside Boelter Hall]]
Wazzan was the recipient in 1966 of a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] at the [[University of Copenhagen]] in [[Denmark]] for studies of magnetic interaction in solids.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A. R. Frank Wazzan |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/ahmed-r-frank-wazzan/ |access-date=2023-12-01 |website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation... |language=en}}</ref>

He was the recipient in 1977 of the "Favorite Professor Award" from the Engineering Society of the University of California.

His paper (with H. Procaccia, and J. David) "Effects of baffling and nonuniform feedwater discharge hole distribution on PWR thermal hydraulics." was awarded "Best Paper" at the Proceedings of International Nuclear Power Plant Thermal Hydraulics and Operations, Taipei City, Taiwan, Republic of China. 1984.

He is recipient of the Gold Medal Award at the First International Meeting on Nuclear Power Plants in Commercial Operations.<ref name="auto" />

Wazzan was an Associate Fellow of the [[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=AIAA Associate Fellows |url=https://www.aiaa.org/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/membership-and-communities/individual-membership/aiaa-membership-grades/aiaa-associate-fellows-roster.pdf?sfvrsn=dd85832d_0 }}</ref> He was a Fellow of the [[American Nuclear Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=American Nuclear Society, 2012 Honors & Awards Recipients |url=https://wx1.ans.org/honors/recipients/docs/ha_presentation_brochure_june2012.pdf |website=American Nuclear Society}}</ref>

On June 29, 2001, Wazzan was honored with a tree dedication and plaque permanently mounted outside Boelter Hall, [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] inscribed "Dean A. R. Frank Wazzan - In Honor of his 15 Years of Leadership and Vision."<ref>See appended photo "Wazzan Plaque Outside Boelter Hall."</ref>
